 Taylor Ardrey USA TODAY Nov. 5, 2026, 2:28 p.m. ET Hear this story More than 175,000 air fryer ovens sold at Target are being recalled due to a burn hazard.
 According to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Gourmia Stainless 9-Slice Digital Air Fryer's doors "unexpectedly close when bumped" while retrieving food. If the door closes, it could burn a person as they use the appliance.
 In the recall notice posted on Nov. 5, the kitchen appliance company said it received 57 reports of the issue. Additionally, they noted 40 incidents of "burns to consumer hands or wrists."
 Here's what we know about the product and what consumers should do next.
 More news: More than 3.6 million ladders recalled. See the affected products USA TODAY Shopping: Shop sales in tech, home, fashion, beauty & more curated by our editors. What product is being recalled?
 According to the agency and Gourmia's website , the product is stainless steel with glass French doors and metal handles:
 Model Number: GTF7530 (found on back)
 Date code: 0126(13) (found on back)
 UPC Code:  810002862779
 Where were the recalled air fryer ovens sold?
 The air fryer ovens, listed at $150, were sold at Target locations and the retailer's website between October 2021 and June 2026.
 What should consumers do if they have the recalled air fryer ovens?
 The CPSC advises consumers to stop using the product and contact Gourmia.
 You can reach out to Gourmia during normal business hours at 888-834-0092 or online on the company website . The company email is  info@gourmia.com.
 Consumers will receive a free repair kit with installation instructions and a magnetic doorstop in the mail.
 Taylor Ardrey is a news reporter for USA TODAY. You can reach her at tardrey@usatodayco.com.
